assertions.assert: Its input is its `<param>`s: it sends itself `bot.ability.vision.description.input` `{image, media_type}` (the original's media.Image, by reference), which its schema checks, so an `image` that is missing or empty sends nothing to the model and answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "Description could not run (error.execution)"}`; nothing reaches the parent before its one answer.

It asks the generate service once, with one user message (the original's DESCRIBE_INSTRUCTIONS as a text part and the image's reference as an image part, the image read from the granted media directory), and answers its parent `bot.ability.vision.description.output` `{description}`, the reply trimmed of white space; then it ends (`done.invoke.<id>` follows the answer).
A reply that is empty once stripped answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "the generator answered with an empty description"}`.

A description of at most 4000 characters (the original's MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS, counted in characters, not bytes) is answered; a longer one is an output its schema refuses and answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "Description produced output that does not match its output schema."}`, the original's invalid-output failure.

A model call that fails answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "Description generator failed: <code>."}`, the generate service's failure code in the message, and an image reference the generate service cannot read rejects its start: `{message: "Description could not run (error.execution)"}`.
